title: Working carbon monoxide and smoke alarms by housing tenure in a rural county: a cross-sectional household survey with test-button verification
abstract: Objective: to estimate the prevalence of working carbon monoxide and smoke alarms by housing tenure and heating type in a rural county. Design: cross-sectional household survey from a stratified two-stage cluster sample of the property roll, January to March 2027, with test-button verification. Primary outcome: a working carbon monoxide alarm in homes with a fuel-burning appliance. Results and conclusions will be written after fieldwork.
introduction: Carbon monoxide deaths cluster in homes without a working alarm, and existing local data come only from households who ask for fire service visits. Retrieved surveys suggest that renters and homes heated with solid fuel or bottled gas are least protected, but no estimate by tenure exists for this county.
methods: About 1,630 addresses in 70 segments are sampled with probability proportional to size within town and rural strata. Fieldworkers visit up to three times, record reported ownership, then test alarms in the hallway and kitchen. Survey-weighted prevalence and a prevalence ratio for rented versus owner-occupied homes are estimated with robust variance.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present response by tenure, weighted prevalence with confidence intervals by tenure and heating type, the renter and owner prevalence ratio, and agreement between reported and working alarms.
discussion: The discussion will compare the county estimates with the retrieved rural and national figures, weigh nonresponse bias, and set out how the giveaway will be retargeted.
limitations: Nonresponse may differ by tenure; bedrooms are not inspected; tenure is reported at the door; one winter only.
conclusion: To be written after fieldwork; it will be limited to prevalence and the tenure comparison and will not claim effects of the giveaway.
summary: STROBE-structured draft with results left empty until fieldwork ends.
